about: The newest reports, by the day each first appeared (the commit that added it). Generated by scripts/build_reports_index.py from reports.json and every topic page and hub.

reports.title: Senior tax work-off
reports.about: Seniors in the work-off fell from 16 in 2010 to 6 in 2025, while the cap rose from $750 to $1,500.

reports.title: Special education grants
reports.about: Special education grants and the circuit breaker paid $1,055,922 in FY2023 and $773,361 in FY2026.

reports.title: Tuition after repayment
reports.about: Of $230,514 a year for an average private placement, Lunenburg keeps $96,943 after the state repays $133,571.

reports.title: Surprise costs
reports.about: A surprise cost is spending above the budget as voted: $1,235,009 over 17 years.

reports.title: Special education reserve fund
reports.about: A special education line spent past its vote in 13 of 17 years, on top of the state repayment the vote counts on. A median bad year of the last five ran $116,811 over; the worst year on record, $223,774. Held once, a reserve costs less than a yearly cushion.

reports.title: Reserve or budget
reports.about: Budgeting the cushion every year raises $2,345,375 more than a reserve covering the same years.

reports.title: Reserve options
reports.about: Seven ways to size the reserve run from $90,554 to $412,397; the law caps it at $541,717.

reports.title: Positions and their funds
reports.about: Of 10 general fund leadership accounts, 2 had any pay moved to or from another fund.

reports.title: Pay moved between funds
reports.about: Journal entries moved $545,630 of general fund pay onto other funds in four years, and $617,530 back.

reports.title: Pay from grants and fees
reports.about: Grants and fee funds paid $7,268,170 of school pay in four years; no account names the job.

reports.title: Move-ins
reports.about: A child in a private placement who moves in is the former town’s cost that year; after 1 April, the next too.

reports.title: Grants for surprises
reports.about: The circuit breaker paid a median $507,832 a year, FY2010 to FY2026; IDEA allocated $437,380 for FY2027.

reports.title: Carried-over orders
reports.about: The general fund carried at most $190,128 of open orders into a new year, and the budget went with them.

reports.title: Special education definition
reports.about: Our rules now count what DESE’s documents count; DESE’s FY2024 report still counts $743,667 more.

reports.title: Grants other districts get
reports.about: Comparison districts won 19 competitive grants Lunenburg did not in FY2026–FY2027; it won 2.

reports.title: Grant allocations compared
reports.about: Lunenburg gets less IDEA per pupil than most comparable districts; Title I tracks its low-income share.

reports.title: Unspent money by fund
reports.about: Fees, lunch and the circuit breaker held $1,692,438 at the end of FY2023; by our count, $1,119,636 by FY2026.

reports.title: The whole school budget
reports.about: The voted school budget is the general fund. Every fund together spent $29,929,041 in FY2026, $3,641,567 more, and these pages show where it came from and which lines it paid.

reports.title: School grants and aid
reports.about: In FY2025 Chapter 70 aid was $8,988,960 and every grant spent $1,196,194: general aid beside restricted money.

reports.title: Paid outside the general fund
reports.about: Funds outside the voted budget spent $16,680,612 in four years: 13.4% of school spending in FY2026.

reports.title: Grant spending by line
reports.about: Grant spending on a voted budget line went from 5.1% in FY2023 to 2.3% in FY2026.

reports.title: Budget lines, all funds
reports.about: In FY2026 other funds spent $4,024,956 beside the general fund; $2,408,319 of it sat on no budget line.

reports.title: Turf field capital plans
reports.about: The schools have put the field in every capital plan of theirs since FY2022; its year kept moving.

reports.title: Surplus suggestions
reports.about: The surplus came from many small leftovers, year after year, not one line; these options follow from that.

reports.title: Inflation and school costs
reports.about: Most of the rise in school spending since FY2009 is inflation: $8.9 million of $10.6 million a year.

reports.title: Upkeep leftover by account
reports.about: Building upkeep left $195,934 in FY2026 on 14 accounts; each card shows what was paid, skipped and released.

reports.title: What upkeep buys
reports.about: Most of building upkeep is steady work: $291,136 to $389,138 a year to payees paid year after year.

reports.title: Usual purchases skipped
reports.about: 10 payees the schools used every year were paid under half as usual in FY2026; 5 got nothing.

reports.title: Upkeep surplus, every dollar
reports.about: Building upkeep left $195,934 in FY2026: $75,660 on one account, the rest on 13 others.

reports.title: Upkeep budget and spending
reports.about: Building upkeep’s budget rose 96% from FY2023 to FY2026; what it spent rose 42%.

reports.title: Under budget twice
reports.about: 6 budget areas came in under every year from FY2023 to FY2026; 11 of 18 did in both FY2025 and FY2026.

reports.title: Surplus, step by step
reports.about: FY2026’s leftover is $482,118 to $718,885, depending on $236,767 of purchase orders still open.

reports.title: Contracted building services
reports.about: Third-party building services left $75,660 in FY2026, after two years of spending past the budget.

reports.title: Building upkeep
reports.about: Building upkeep’s budget nearly doubled in four years, $332,016 to $652,033, while spending grew 42%. These pages show what it buys, and where the difference sits.

reports.title: Special education burndown
reports.about: In FY2026 the circuit breaker paid $4,005 from July to May, then $333,495 in one June entry.

reports.title: Budget burndown
reports.about: By the end of March FY2026 had 40.2% of its budget left, against 33.0% and 32.6% in FY2023 and FY2024.

reports.title: Special education, all funds
reports.about: Special education spending passed its voted budget every year, and other funds paid the difference.

reports.title: Special education providers
reports.about: Three payees took 66.5% of special education vendor payments; Keystone was paid 4.3 times as much by FY2026.

reports.title: Teachers on the scale
reports.about: In calendar 2025, 56 of 90 teachers we matched were paid at least the master’s top step.

reports.title: Teacher pay compared
reports.about: Of 5 FY2026 salary schedules compared, Lunenburg’s top step was lowest in the bachelor’s and master’s lanes.

reports.title: Pay or headcount
reports.about: FY2025 had 15.2 fewer teachers than FY2009, but each cost $36,331 more; the teachers line rose $2,887,749.

reports.title: Spending by type over time
reports.about: School spending, all funds, went from $19,446,453 in FY2009 to $30,031,242 in FY2025.

reports.title: Growth by spending type
reports.about: Each against its own FY2009 cost: insurance and retirement grew 83%, paras 89%, teachers 39%, all 54%.
